transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I think we all know P-2 failed this morning and we've got production areas without cooling. Before we discuss any temporary fixes like hose connections, I want to make sure we go through our standard pre-work review covering process, maintenance, and EHS findings. I also need to remind everyone that we don't use temporary connections unless the installation, access, and isolation controls are properly recorded first. Let's talk through what we're dealing with and what options we have.

transcript.text: I need to share something important for this discussion. My process calculation for today's Reactor R batch shows it requires exactly 400 kW of cooling and a supply temperature no higher than 8 degrees Celsius. I completed this during the batch review but haven't entered it in the production control record yet. This is critical for evaluating whether any temporary cooling arrangement can support the reactor batch.

transcript.text: I need to share what I confirmed this morning with the rental provider. A temporary chiller rated at exactly 250 kW can arrive today, and it requires exactly 6 hours for installation. I should note that the vendor confirmation for the rental chiller is not yet attached to the maintenance work order, so we'll need to get that documented as part of our pre-work review.

Thanks everyone for sharing those findings. Let me make sure I understand the situation clearly before we decide on next steps.

Jon, you're telling us the reactor batch needs 400 kW of cooling at 8°C or colder, but that calculation isn't in the production control record yet. We need that documented as part of our pre-work review.

Priya, so we have two potential cooling sources: a 250 kW rental chiller that takes 6 hours to install, and Pump P-1 which can provide 300 kW after isolating Valve V-17. But the vendor confirmation isn't attached to the work order yet.

Owen, EHS requires 1.2 meters clearance with barriers and a fire watch for the hose route crossing the access lane, and your inspection notes aren't filed with the work permit yet.

So the combined capacity from both sources would be 550 kW, which exceeds the 400 kW requirement. But we have several documentation gaps to close before we can authorize anything: Jon's calculation needs to go in the production control record, Priya's vendor confirmation needs to be on the work order, and Owen's inspection notes need to be filed with the work permit. Also, any temporary hose installation, access, and isolation controls must be recorded before use.

Can everyone commit to getting those documents filed so we can complete the pre-work review and make a decision? I don't want to authorize any temporary connections until all of that is in order.
